source_text.body:
Run a solo SaaS with an agent that texts you
A solo founder of a hosted SaaS has Claude Code write most code and text them when it needs input, taking instructions by phone.
·
Jul 1, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
A solo founder running a hosted SaaS says Claude Code writes most of the code, but the key setup was a control layer for unattended runs. They used background hooks so the agent long-polled Telegram, accepted instructions and replied in the same thread, and only interrupted for approvals, real errors, or decisions; they also routed tasks across cheap, mid, and top models and loaded external tool definitions only when needed.
How it went
The founder says this shift from constant supervision to interrupt-only operation changed how much they ship more than prompting tricks did. The main shortcoming was tuning the interrupt threshold, which took weeks because early versions either pinged too often or stayed quiet on things they wanted to catch.
Worth knowing
The biggest catch was not coding the hooks but spending weeks calibrating what truly counts as “needs a human.”
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Work on my codebase at [path] to ship [feature or bug list], and run the tests as you go. When you need a decision or hit something you can't resolve, send me a short message at [text or chat channel] with your question and options, then wait for my reply. Finish each task with a summary of changes and a branch or pull request, and don't deploy to production without my approval.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCode/comments/1v5cb59/i_stopped_opening_the_terminal_to_check_on_my
